analysis.title: Bumper jobs report keeps December hike on track
key_insights: October nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000, better than expected. Upward revisions to the prior two months lifted the three-month average to 137,000 per month, the highest since late spring.
The unemployment rate rounded down to 4.1% in October (4.14%, from 4.17% in September). The over-25 unemployment rate has stayed within a three-tenths of a percentage point range for over two years.

Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% m/m. With upward revisions, the year-over-year gain is 3.1%. Services wage growth slowed to a cycle-low 2.8%, while goods-producing wage growth rose to 4.2%, led by construction.
JPM says market-based odds of a December Fed hike rose after the report. It views yesterday's questioning about a December hike as overdone and still expects a hike next month.
After December, JPM thinks it would take an inflation surprise to move faster than a quarterly pace. It adds there is a lot to assess between now and the March FOMC meeting.
Private payrolls rose 159,000, the most since March. Government jobs rose 6,000 as volatility in government employment tempered.
Manufacturing jobs rose 19,000 and have increased for six straight months, and now sit just above their January 2025 level. Construction fell 3,000, all in residential.

Jobs in nonresidential construction, associated contractors and heavy and civil engineering rose 165,000 over the past year, only 0.1% of total employment. JPM says this thin job base may partly explain this week's popular backlash against data centers.

Professional, scientific and technical services added 33,000 jobs. This category includes many subcategories at the center of AI job-loss concerns, and JPM calls it a glimmer of hope that AI-related job loss is far off, while cautioning against over-reading one month.
Health care jobs rose 42,000, the best since March. JPM says the new Congress may try to reverse planned federal health care payment cuts.
The household survey showed employment up 463,000 and unemployed down 41,000. Participation rose a tenth to 61.9%, still six tenths below its level of last October.

Median unemployment duration rose to a cycle-high 11.9 weeks, which JPM attributes to a low-hire, low-fire environment. U-6 rose three tenths to 7.9%, mostly from part-time workers who want full-time jobs.
JPM says consumers are still supported by steady labor income growth and the economic backdrop remains benign, even as expenditure-side data point to slower GDP growth this quarter.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Better than expected and a rebound in job growth, supporting the case for a December Fed hike.
Highest since late spring after upward revisions to the prior two months.
Edged lower, helped by a decline in teenage unemployment. Over-20 unemployment was stable.
Down a tenth from an upward-revised September. Services wage growth slowed to 2.8%.
Up a tenth and still recovering from the sharp fall earlier this year.
Up three tenths, mostly from more part-time workers wanting full-time jobs.
Steady for a third straight month, recovered from mid-2025 weakness.
JPM sees the data as supporting a hike and thinks only an inflation surprise would justify a faster-than-quarterly pace afterward.

risk_factors: An inflation surprise could push the Fed to move faster than a quarterly pace after December.
Median unemployment duration at a cycle-high 11.9 weeks and U-6 at 7.9% point to a low-hire, low-fire market.
Expenditure-side data indicate a step-down in GDP growth this quarter.
Policy-related pullback in data center spending, though JPM expects limited impact on job growth.
vol_and_positioning: JPM says the Committee should stay calm about an equity market move of a handful of percentage points, so the December hike should not be derailed by it.
Market-based odds of a December Fed hike increased after the jobs data.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM argues the data show little need to insure against downside labor market risks and that more restraint looks warranted, so a December hike is on track.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets questioned a December hike a day earlier, after an equity market move of a handful of percentage points, and expenditure-side data point to slower GDP growth this quarter.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An equity market move larger than a handful of percentage points, or labor market data pointing to downside risks, would challenge the hike call. JPM says an inflation surprise would be needed to move faster than quarterly after December.

theme_stances.key_argument: The data suggest little need to insure against downside labor market risks, so JPM continues to look for a hike next month.
theme_stances.evidence: We continue to look for hike next month.
